Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150329
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32546 of 2024

Applicant :- Rajesh Singh @ Rajkumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Kartikey Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- Pankaj Sharma,G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Amit Kumar Rai, Advocate filed his Power on behalf of the informant which is taken on record.

2. Heard Kartikey Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Amit Kumar Rai, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.394 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Mathura,
during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant with the name of Raj Kumar and two others and according to the FIR, from the vehicle of the applicant in the year 2019, an accident occurred and in that accident one person lost his life and FIR was lodged under Section 304-A, 279 IPC and in that case applicant on the basis of the false and Rajesh Singh @ Rajkumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148263143/
1 fake bail bonds came out from the jail and his vehicle was also released on the basis of the fake document but entire allegation levelled against the applicant is totally false and at the time of the alleged incident, he was in jail and his Advocates and other persons arranged the bail bonds and,
therefore, it cannot be said that applicant committed any fraud and cheating.
5. He further submits that apart from the present case and the case under Section 304-A, 279 IPC there is no other criminal history of the applicant.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submits that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 09.03.2024 i.e. for more than six months.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that since beginning applicant is playing fraud and sometimes he disclosed himself as a driver of the vehicle and sometimes he claimed himself owner of the vehicle but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that when bail application was filed then applicant was in jail.

8. They also could not dispute the fact that except the present case and case under Section 304-A,
279 IPC, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 09.03.2024 i.e. for more than six months.

9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
10.

Considering the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant and the fact that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 09.03.2024 i.e. for more than six months and no exception could be brought on record on the basis of which instant bail application can be rejected, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Rajesh Singh @ Rajkumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

sentences.text: 13. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
